title: Wanting music, quitting school, and buying an Albert-system clarinet
summary: Youngest of ten, he could not afford lessons, left high school to work, bought a clarinet instead of a trumpet, and still plays the Albert system; born April 14, 1907.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: No, I moved here when I was about six years old, my folks moved here. And I guess from the age of seven I wanted to play music. And being the youngest of ten, by the time it got to me they couldn't afford it. And my sister studied piano and voice for about fourteen years. And I told them I wanted to play piano at the time, and no, go outside and play, you bother me, you're too much trouble and all this and that. So finally when I got old enough, my mind was so set on it that I quit high school to go to work so I could buy a musical instrument. And I went to get a trumpet, and it cost too much money so I bought the clarinet. And I'm still playing it.
That's funny. That's an odd thing. What kind of clarinet did you start off on?
Well the Albert system, which I still play, is no use changing now, I'm kind of late.
Well, I like the tone. Sounds good.

Well I don't think I could do any more, any better with the BAME system. And when I started the Albert was still quite popular. Most of the boys who were playing a long time now just changed over, but they sacrificed a lot of tone for easy fingering.
What day were you born exactly? April 14th, 1907. So you're relatively young to be playing an Albert actually, most of the guys now who are in your generation are playing BAME.
